summary: Umatilla NF lookout near Elgin: an 83-foot L-4 tower built in 1948 replaced an older one, and a falling tree destroyed it in 1990.

facts.design: 83-foot treated timber tower with an L-4 cab (1948); earlier a 30-foot pole platform with tent, then a 50-foot L-4 tower
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1990 when a tree fell across the guy wires; no source describes what remains at the site

staffing.status: staffed through 1990; named personnel include Mrs. Elsie Ralph (Forest Lookouts) or Mrs. James Ralph (firelookout.com) in 1943, Dean McKenzie in 1950, and Bob Faust in 1968

events.note: Forest Lookouts quotes an August 1926 account of a 50-foot tower found framed and ready to raise; the register and firelookout.com date the 50-foot tower to 1935
50-foot L-4 tower, per firetower.org and firelookout.com
A 1943 passage quoted by Forest Lookouts says the old tower had decayed to the point where it was no longer safe for use
Mrs. Elsie Ralph (Forest Lookouts) or Mrs. James Ralph (firelookout.com) was the lookout
Old tower condemned and razed, per the Forest Lookouts quote; the history flags the date as questionable. A 1947 item says it toppled in 1946
Lightning fire a quarter mile east of Spout Springs, spotted and put out by lookout Dean McKenzie
Bob Faust listed as a lookout
A tree fell across the guy wires and destroyed the tower
Date registered August 21, 2011 on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register

corrections.why: The 30-foot figure belongs to the 1920s pole platform with tent. The tower standing from 1948 was 83 feet (25.3 m).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com date the 50-foot tower to 1935; Forest Lookouts quotes an August 1926 account of one being raised. Both dates are given in the story and neither is chosen.
Forest Lookouts gives Mrs. Elsie Ralph and firelookout.com gives Mrs. James Ralph for the same 1943 entry. The story uses the name given by Forest Lookouts and notes the variant.

notes_for_editor: Build date of the first 50-foot tower conflicts (1926 vs 1935), and the 1943 Ralph name differs between sources. The brief's height_m of 9.1 is the 1920s platform; the 1948 tower was 83 ft. No source describes remains at the site or public access; the sno-park page is not tied to the lookout. The 1944 demolition date is flagged as questionable by its source. The editor should decide whether to mention the 1926 date alongside 1935.
